description: This line plot, labeled as Figure 8(b), illustrates the performance on the Llama2 model, measuring the accuracy (ACC %) of knowledge probing after editing against the co-occurrence number of the edited facts. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to 10^3, with major tick marks at 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", is on a linear scale ranging from 60% to 80%, with major tick marks at 60, 65, 70, 75, and 80. Six distinct methods are plotted, each represented by a unique color, marker, and line style as defined in the legend: "Base" (black line with circle markers), "FT" (blue line with triangle-down markers), "IKE" (red line with triangle-up markers), "MEND" (brown line with diamond markers), "MEMIT" (purple line with square markers), and "ROME" (green line with square markers). All methods show an increasing trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number grows. The "Base" model starts at approximately 62% accuracy and rises to about 67%. The "FT" method begins around 63% and increases to roughly 69%. The "IKE" method starts near 65% and climbs to approximately 70%. The "MEND" method begins at about 67% and reaches around 74%. The "MEMIT" method starts at approximately 66% and increases to about 73%. The "ROME" method consistently performs the best, starting at roughly 72% and rising to approximately 78%.
